labels.label: theo:universality_sphere

hypotheses.paper: Phi_i in SO_{d+1}(R) acting on S^d (l.303)
hypotheses.note: Phi : Fin p -> SO n acting by x |-> Ax on RoundSphere n, n = d + 1

hypotheses.paper: S^d a sphere of positive dimension (implicit in l.297)
hypotheses.note: 2 <= n, i.e. d >= 1; needed: on S^0 the density form fails (EGF.not_universalitySphereDense_zero; EGF.universalitySphereDense_iff: it holds iff d >= 1)

hypotheses.paper: the group generated by the Phi_i dense in SO(d,R) (l.836)
hypotheses.note: Dense (Subgroup.closure (Set.range Phi)) in SO n with the subspace topology, read in SO(d+1), the group the rotations of S^d live in (C-32/C-33 index slip)

hypotheses.paper: the set of Phi_i stable under inverse (l.836)
hypotheses.note: not used: the a.e.-stabilizer of a set is a subgroup
the route is ergodicity of SO(n) on the sphere plus Mathlib's aeconst_of_dense_aestabilizer_smul
the rich model contains the uniform kernel of the given Phi
any family F; isometrySphericalFamily M of a rich model is an instance

hypotheses.paper: (unstated) the model realizes alpha = 1/p and outflows dense in the non-negative cone of L2(sigma)

findings: main.tex:305 with l.307 and l.836 (C-28 sphere half, C-49): Theorem 3.6 holds on every S^d, d >= 1, when the Phi_i generate a dense subgroup of SO(d+1) and the model is rich (C-31): EGF.universality_sphere. The algebraic coefficients (l.307, l.836), the inverse-stability (l.836) and the spectral gap (l.307) are not needed. For d = 1 this was EGF.universality_sphere_one_of_dense; universality_sphere covers every d >= 1 uniformly, so the corrected Theorem 3.6 of C-28 and the corrected l.307 of C-49 are anchored for d >= 2.

The route that replaces l.836's spectral gap (C-32's last clause): SO(n), n >= 2, acts transitively on S^{n-1} (EGF.exists_rotSphere_eq, two reflections), hence sigma is sigma(S) times the orbit pushforward of Haar (Fubini, EGF.sphereVolume_eq_smul_map_orbit), hence SO(n) acts ergodically (EGF.ergodicSMul_rotSphere, through the ergodicity of left translation on SO(n)); a dense subgroup of a group acting continuously and ergodically acts ergodically (Mathlib's aeconst_of_dense_aestabilizer_smul): EGF.ae_const_of_dense_rotations. For n = 1 transitivity fails (EGF.not_transitive_rotSphere_one).

main.tex:305 on S^2 (the sphere of the experiments, l.496): the printed Theorem 3.6 is false there too (C-31, extending EGF.not_universalitySpherePrinted_one from S^1): the rotations of cosine 3/5 about the third and first axes and their inverses (EGF.so3Witness) meet l.836 (entries 0, 1, 3/5, ±4/5; stable under inverse; dense in SO(3), EGF.so3Witness_dense) and the constant-heads model at them is not epsilon-universal: EGF.not_universalitySpherePrinted_two.

main.tex:307-308 ('the main Theorem of breuillard2003dense allows to build a dense subgroup of SO_d(R) with two generators and algebraic coefficients. Therefore, EGF are universal on spheres with p=4 ... the two generators and their inverse'): on S^2 the two generators are explicit and need no citation: R_z(theta), R_x(theta) with cos theta = 3/5 generate a dense subgroup of SO(3) (Euler angles EGF.so3_euler, and theta/2pi irrational by Niven), and with their inverses (p = 4) the L2 model is epsilon-universal (EGF.universality_sphere_witness_three). For S^d, d >= 3, the existence of such a pair still rests on breuillard2003dense (not formalized). The index SO_d of l.307 is SO_{d+1} for S^d (C-33).

Sharpness of d >= 1: on S^0 = {±1} the density form is false, trivially (SO(1) is trivial, so every family is dense, and the identity is not ergodic): EGF.not_universalitySphereDense_zero; EGF.universalitySphereDense_iff: the density form holds on S^d iff d >= 1. The paper's spheres are presumably of positive dimension; recorded for completeness.
questions: main.tex:297 'S^d': read with d >= 1 (RoundSphere n, 2 <= n). At d = 0 the corrected statement fails (EGF.not_universalitySphereDense_zero); the paper never considers S^0.

main.tex:836 'dense in SO(d,R)' for rotations of S^d in SO_{d+1}: read as dense in SO(d+1), the group the rotations live in (the reading of EGF/SphereFamilies.lean, C-32's index slip); 'the group generated by' read as the subgroup Subgroup.closure (range Phi). In a compact group the closure of the generated semigroup is already a group, so the semigroup reading gives the same condition (not formalized).
main.tex:308 'well-chosen (Phi_i)_{i=1}^4' read as 'there exist': exhibited on S^2 (EGF.so3Witness) and, with p = 2, on S^1 (EGF.so2Witness); not exhibited for S^d, d >= 3.

corrections.proposed_status: proved (sphere half: the density form for every d >= 1)
corrections.note: The registered corrected Theorem 3.6 ('the Phi_i generate a dense subgroup of SO_{d+1}(R)', with C-31's richness) is EGF.universality_sphere for every n = d + 1 >= 2, and UniversalitySphereDense d is that sentence as a Prop, true iff d >= 1. The corrected l.836 ('the group then acts ergodically on S^d') is EGF.isGroupErgodic_sphereRotGroup_of_dense. The tori half waits on T-egf-tori-minimal.

The d >= 2 anchor of the corrected l.307 ('frozen and generate a dense subgroup of SO_{d+1}(R) ... neither a spectral gap nor algebraic coefficients are needed'): EGF.universality_sphere (no algebraicity, no inverse-stability, no spectral gap); non-vacuous at d = 2 by EGF.universality_sphere_witness_three. The refutation stays EGF.not_universality_sphere_identity.

corrections.proposed_status: proved (no change: its last clause now has a density anchor for every d >= 1)
corrections.note: Last sentence of the corrected text ('Theorem 3.6 does not use a spectral gap: it rests on the ergodicity of the group generated by the Phi_i'): the density that gives that ergodicity is now proved sufficient for every d >= 1, so the sentence could name it.
New anchor beyond the dispatch: the printed Theorem 3.6 over models (EGF.UniversalitySpherePrinted 2) is refuted on S^2 as well, at EGF.so3Witness, which meets l.836.

kb_proposals: SO(n) instances, named as AUDIT-1 of T-egf-families-sphere asked (EGF.instIsTopologicalGroupSO, instCompactSpaceSO, instSecondCountableTopologySO, instMeasurableSpaceSO := borel, instBorelSpaceSO; soHaar n := haarMeasure ⊤ with IsHaarMeasure, IsProbabilityMeasure, IsMulRightInvariant): SecondCountableTopology (SO n) is not found by infer_instance (SO n is a coerced Submonoid and Matrix has no SecondCountableTopology instance): build the matrix one locally by inferInstanceAs (SecondCountableTopology (Fin n → Fin n → ℝ)) and apply TopologicalSpace.Subtype.secondCountableTopology _ explicitly. Right invariance on a compact group: Measure.isMulInvariant_eq_smul_of_compactSpace (map (· * g) μ) μ (isMulLeftInvariant_map_mul_right is an instance), then evaluate at univ.

Ergodicity of a transitive compact-group action without a homogeneous-space API: Fubini on G × X (Measure.prod_apply and prod_apply_symm of {p | p.1 • p.2 ∈ s}; transitivity and measure_preimage_mul_right) gives σ = σ(X) • (g ↦ g • x₀)₊ Haar, so the orbit map is quasi-measure-preserving; a.e.-invariant sets pull back to a.e.-invariant subsets of G, and Mathlib's instance ErgodicSMul G G μ (Dynamics/Ergodic/Action/Regular.lean) finishes (EGF.ergodicSMul_rotSphere). Then dense subgroups: closure (range Φ) ≤ MulAction.aestabilizer via Set.preimage_smul and inv_mem, and aeconst_of_dense_aestabilizer_smul (InnerRegular of volume.toSphere is found automatically).

Transitivity of SO(n) on S^{n−1} (n ≥ 2): Submodule.reflection_sub sends x to y, Submodule.det_reflection gives (−1)^finrank Kᗮ (orthogonal_orthogonal, finrank_span_singleton), a second reflection in a nonzero v ⊥ y fixes y (Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot with finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal); a linear isometry of determinant 1 is an element of SO n by LinearMap.toMatrix in EuclideanSpace.basisFun (LinearIsometryEquiv.toMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup, LinearMap.det_toMatrix, toMatrix_mulVec_repr, OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis_repr_apply): EGF.exists_SO_of_det_eq_one.

SO(3) computations: rotZ/rotX membership by ext + fin_cases + simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_three] + nlinarith [cos_sq_add_sin_sq]; Euler angles via the third column (arccos of A 2 2, then an angle for (−A12, A02)/sin b, EGF.exists_angle through Complex.arg) and the stabilizer of e₃ (EGF.exists_rotZ_of_fix: nlinarith on the entries of B Bᵀ = 1 and det_fin_three); density by mem_topologicalClosure_zpowers (EGF/SphereFamilies.lean) on both one-parameter subgroups. Pitfalls: Matrix.mem_orthogonalGroup_iff takes n and R explicitly; EuclideanSpace.single_apply is deprecated for PiLp.single_apply; Mathlib has a Module (Matrix n n R) (n → R) instance, so A • v on EuclideanSpace already means A *ᵥ v (through WithLp.instSMul), a possible second path to an action on the sphere should Mathlib ever add one.
